memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The LORD said to Moses: 'When anyone is unfaithful to the LORD by sinning unintentionally in regard to any of the LORD's holy things, they are to bring to the LORD as a penalty a ram from the flock, one without defect and of the proper value in silver, according to the sanctuary shekel. It is a guilt offering.'" - Lev 5:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A new offering appears here — the guilt offering, or reparation offering. Its focus is different from the sin offering. This one deals with damage done, with something taken that must be paid back.

And the first case God addresses is the LORD's holy things — sacred property, the tithe, things dedicated to God's use.

Notice the word unfaithful. Not merely careless. When a person treated what belonged to God as though it were ordinary, God called it unfaithfulness — the language of a broken relationship, not just a broken rule.

Israel could be casual with God's things. So can we. We borrow from what we had committed to give. We take time we had set aside for God and spend it elsewhere. Small erosions, rarely deliberate.

Notice also that this required both a ram and a valuation in silver. Forgiveness and repayment. God did not permit the worshipper to say sorry and keep what he had taken.

Malachi later confronted Israel about exactly this, asking, "Will a mere mortal rob God?" (Mal 3:8). It is a sobering question — and one worth asking gently of ourselves.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I grown casual with something I once set apart for God?
2. Is there anything I have taken back from God that I need to return?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me where I have treated what is Yours as though it were mine. Make me faithful with what You have entrusted to me. Amen.
